examples.vi: Màn trình diễn của cô ấy trên sân khấu thực sự rất ấn tượng.

senses.vi: người đáng nể; điều đặc biệt

senses.definition: a moderate amount or degree of a quality, especially in 'something of a'

examples.en: The sudden cancellation was something of a shock.
examples.vi: Việc hủy bỏ đột ngột phần nào là một cú sốc.

senses.definition: a special or attractive quality that is difficult to describe clearly

examples.en: She has a certain something that makes everyone like her.
examples.vi: Cô ấy có một nét cuốn hút khiến ai cũng yêu mến.

senses.vi: sức hút khó tả; nét cuốn hút

examples: I must have forgotten to pack something, but I can't think what.
I have something for you in my bag.
wiktionary.gloss: An uncertain or unspecified thing; one thing.
wiktionary.vi: cái gì; gì; một cái gì đó

examples: The performance was something of a disappointment.
That child is something of a genius.
wiktionary.gloss: A quality to a moderate degree.

examples: She has a certain something.
wiktionary.gloss: A talent or quality that is difficult to specify.

examples: He's really something! I've never heard such a great voice.
She's quite something. I can't believe she would do such a mean thing.
wiktionary.gloss: Somebody who or something that is superlative or notable in some way.

blocks.etymology: From Middle English somþyng, some-thing, som thing, sum thinge, sum þinge, from Old English sum þing (literally “some thing”), equivalent to some + thing. Compare Old English āwiht (“something”, literally “some thing, any thing”), Swedish någonting (“something”, literally “some thing, any thing”).

senses.definition: used before words like 'like' to mean roughly, approximately, or partly

examples.en: The new jacket costs something like fifty dollars.
examples.vi: Chiếc áo khoác mới có giá khoảng chừng năm mươi đô la.

senses.vi: khoảng chừng; hơi hơi; na ná

senses.definition: used before an adjective to emphasize that a feeling or situation is very strong

examples.en: My back has been hurting something terrible all day.
examples.vi: Lưng tôi đau kinh khủng suốt cả ngày hôm nay.

vi_block: Something like (thông tục) mới thật là.
Hơi hơi, gọi là, chút ít.

examples: The baby looks something like his father.
wiktionary.gloss: Somewhat; to a degree.

examples: I miss them something terrible/rotten. (I miss them terribly)
wiktionary.gloss: Used to adverbialise a following adjective

examples: What was the something the pilot saw, the something worth killing for?

idioms.gloss: Something is not right, seriously amiss, especially when leading to suspicion of motive.
idioms.phrase: something is rotten in the state of Denmark

idioms.gloss: Or something like that. Used to indicate the possibility that the preceding word or phrase is vague or not exactly correct in its applicability.
To conceal a problem (usually an embarrassing or illegal one) expediently, rather than remedy it thoroughly.
To proceed to do something as soon as possible, especially so as to have something unpleasant behind oneself.
To assign responsibility for (something) to (someone).
idioms.phrase: lay something at the feet of

idioms.gloss: Uttered after acquiring new knowledge.
idioms.phrase: you learn something new every day

idioms.gloss: To reject some act in a spiteful manner.
One cannot expect to receive some benefit if one does not pay for it in some way or does not face a counterbalancing hazard or harm.
idioms.phrase: you don't get something for nothing

idioms.gloss: Doing something mischievous or scheming.
To apply (some instrument or implement) to (something else, to undertake a task or attack upon it, usually vigorously).
To cope with something unfortunate without much effort; to accept or manage difficulties well.
To compare something with a similar thing to give a clearer, more accurate idea.
To have gained an insight that could lead to future success.
To aggressively and persistently force an opinion, belief or idea upon a person (especially if they lack interest or have an opposing viewpoint).
To transform (an object or person) into something worthwhile.
To opt to have winnings staked as another wager, typically on the same outcome, rather than paid out.
To accept and deal with something (an event, etc.) as it occurs, with a composed state of mind.
To become successful on one's own initiative.
To know from a reliable source (that).
Intensely or extremely; badly; in the worst way.
